Definition: from a derivative of σκέπας (a covering; perhaps akin to the base of G4649 through the idea of noticeableness); clothing:--raiment.
BiblicalUsage: Skepasma is raiment, a covering, and it appears once, in the contentment Paul commends: having food and raiment, let us be therewith content.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe food and raiment are enough, because Paul sets the line at what the body needs and calls the rest a snare.
